correctness.rationale: The geometric series gives the exact Zak multiplier, and its symmetric hyperbolic representation is affine in sinh²(a|x−1/2|). The conditional variable change yields the exact law for all a>0. Monotonicity establishes all critical levels; Hessian normal forms at the unique zero and saddle give endpoint and logarithmic constants; one-sided seam expansions produce sharp square-root coefficients; an exact golden-ratio quadratic gives the unique crossover. A separately executed standalone checker verifies the algebra, mean and local Hessian at several parameter values; the analytical proof covers all real parameters. No assertion about ordinary trace-class density is made.

value.rationale: The normalized spectral law is a natural operator-conditioning invariant unavailable from merely knowing the Zak zero or frame set. The full one-dimensional law and global critical-value census reveal a parameter-driven exchange between a logarithmic van Hove saddle and a cusp created by window nonsmoothness, at an exact golden-ratio constant. The sharp lower/upper density constants and distinct edge exponents quantify spectral mass, with plausible use in regularized critical Gabor inversion. The result is a complete, parameter-uniform natural classification rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
